ruling: the plant term re-scoped at the seat level: a live-plant miss voids the seat, not the round. The blind seat's ballot is discarded; the slot is re-drawn once (fresh seat, fresh plant); the round is valid when it holds five caught ballots. Unanimity is preserved where it matters: every counted ballot caught its plant. Broken-judge = a slot whose re-draw also misses, or two slots missing in one round. ... Then re-draw round 5's seat 2 and proceed — the art was passing (4 not-below, 1 below, no strong regression).
supersedes: a correct plant missed still voids [the round] — Rafe, 2026-09-08
_why_the_transitional_clause_applies: Round 5 was voided under the OLD rule for something that is no longer a round-level
fault: ONE seat missing ONE live plant.
lamp-clip-figure.png   seats 2, 4       CAUGHT 1 of 2   <- seat 2, one live miss
Under the new rule that discards seat 2's BALLOT and re-draws the SLOT once. The clause
is narrow by construction: it excuses EXACTLY ONE live miss. Two or more is
broken-judge under the old rule and the new one alike, and no marker excuses it.
⚠ IT DOES NOT DECIDE THE OUTCOME, IT ONLY LETS THE RE-DRAW HAPPEN. If the re-draw also
misses, the seat-level term raises broken-judge on the spot — a slot that misses twice
with a fresh seat and a fresh plant is the judging layer, not the draw.
